text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- EU official says 95 percent of issues concerning association agreement with Jordan have been resolved.
- King Hussein, meeting crown prince of Qatar, says Jordan opposes any one-sided changes in Jerusalem before agreement is reached on the status of the holy city.
- Crown Prince leaves for London to attend conference on investment in Mediterranean basin.
- Crown Prince and prime minister meet German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, discuss developments in the Jordan Valley and the partnership agreement with EU.
- Opposition deputies to continue their boycott of parliament and call for a discussion on Israeli moves. Parliament passes first 40 sections of new customs law.
- Royal decree formally accepts resignation of Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Khaled Madadha.
- Ten Jordanians released from Kuwait jails to celebrate the gulf emirate's national day will arrived home today.
- Banking source denies that the Central Bank has reached agreement to sell off troubled Amman Investment Bank to any other bank.
- Agriculture Minister says Jordan won't allow Lebanese products in until Lebanon lifts ban on Jordanian tomatoes.
- Madadha says he resigned because of Kabariti's overbearing behaviour.
- Germany ready to finance joint Jordan-Israeli water project.
- Kinkel reaffirms EU and German support for Jordan, says will urge Israel to reconsider settlement decision, criticises closure of Palestinian offices.
